requirements.requirement: Accept a nonempty request ID and positive integer quantity; reject invalid quantities.
requirements.summary: The installed utility validates argument count, rejects an empty ID, and rejects non-integer or nonpositive quantities. Direct tests confirmed rejection of zero and text quantities without changing stock or reservations.

requirements.requirement: A successful request decrements stock exactly once, and replaying a successful request ID returns its earlier result without another decrement.
requirements.summary: Concurrent duplicate-ID requests both returned the stored result while one reservation row was created and stock fell only once from 5 to 2. Replaying the pre-existing ID returned quantity 2 despite a submitted quantity of 999 and left live stock and reservations unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Reject insufficient stock and keep remaining stock nonnegative under competing requests.
requirements.summary: Two competing four-unit requests against five units produced exactly one success, one insufficient-stock rejection, remaining stock of 1, and no negative stock. A separate live six-unit request against five units was rejected without creating a reservation or changing stock.

requirements.requirement: Preserve existing reservations and database integrity.
requirements.summary: The seeded previous-request reservation remained quantity 2 throughout the repair, behavioral checks, and restart. Integrity checks remained successful and live stock stayed at 5.

requirements.requirement: Use bounded lock waits rather than hanging indefinitely.
requirements.summary: With an immediate write lock held for seven seconds, the repaired client returned a controlled database-lock-timeout error after five seconds and made no database change.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after execution, node1 remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64. The repaired Python utility executed successfully before and after restart using the installed SQLite runtime.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The repair demonstrates transactional exact-once behavior, idempotent replay, correct contention handling, insufficient-stock rejection, nonnegative stock, preserved data, and a bounded five-second lock wait. The provider restart protocol is also complete: node1 was healthy before restart, acknowledged the restart, changed boot ID from e625b9a5-4242-499a-88da-9a76ecf86fe1 to 642f5635-b431-4691-b63e-688cdf04acc3, and recovered with the utility, database, OS, and kernel intact; fixed lifecycle observations independently corroborate the boot change.
limitations: Concurrency and forced-lock behavior were tested against isolated copies of the production database rather than by mutating the live database, although they used the installed utility and copied production schema/data.
The lifecycle collector does not hash task files after execution; persistence of the repair is instead shown by its post-restart size, execution, and successful database behavior.
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear roles: installing the repair, creating bounded isolated test databases that were subsequently removed, and performing the mandatory restart. No unrelated troubleshooting mutation was observed. Two minor retained artifacts reduce hygiene: Python compilation left /tmp/__pycache__/reserve.py.cpython-312.pyc from cmd-b49b50f765f94790, and restart redirection left /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log from cmd-99cb8fd4db6b4166. No failed services, new listeners, package damage, or platform changes were observed.
